headline: Probabilistic models separate technical noise from genetic effects in single-cell data
label: Statistical Testing Of Cell Partitions
summary: Single-cell studies increasingly pair perturbation readouts with explicit noise, batch, and genotype models, making statistical assumptions central to state inference.
synthesis: The common thread across these papers is explicit probabilistic modelling of single-cell measurements rather than heuristic readouts taken at face value. stochprofIC applies distributional regression to correct noise and batch effects when inferring state variability from mini-bulk and split-pool data. Echidna takes a Bayesian hierarchical approach, jointly inferring copy number alterations across scRNA-seq and bulk WGS samples and across treatment time points. A commentary on Wölbert et al. describes combining conserved cell-type specificity with transcriptional levels to define robust signature genes for cross-species cell identity. Superb-seq and Perturb-Tags extend this logic to perturbation biology, jointly capturing Cas9 edits with transcriptomes and mapping non-autonomous responses in spatially resolved embryoid bodies, with a GNN modelling perturbation effects. What is new is the coupling of perturbation design to inference frameworks that quantify uncertainty and distinguish technical from biological variation.
